sentences.text: Alistipes shahii is a commensal bacterium of the human gut and belongs to the genus Alistipes in the family Rikenellaceae, phylum Bacteroidetes.
It produces indole from tryptophan using tryptophanase, the rate-limiting step of microbial indole production in the intestine.

A study reported that lower abundance of this species lowered intestinal indole in irritable bowel syndrome patients and model mice, describing a gut-brain pathway through hippocampal indole-AhR signalling.
In a bread trial, Alistipes shahii increased significantly after intake of sourdough bread compared with baker's yeast bread.
In a preclinical mouse model, administration of Alistipes shahii improved the efficacy of oncolytic adenovirus therapy.
